# Jearon Wong — Protocol Architect for the Agent Era

Site: https://www.jearonwong.com/

Jearon Wong is the Protocol Architect for the Agent Era.

Execution is not Delivery.

AI agents will not become real infrastructure until execution becomes accountable delivery.

AI agent governance, multi-agent accountability, and production AI agent delivery require more than execution frameworks. AI Agent Lifecycle names the missing governance layer. Agentic Delivery defines the standard. MPLP is the protocol path.

AI Agent Lifecycle defines the accountable lifecycle of agent work from intent to accepted outcome.

Agentic Delivery names the missing layer between agent execution and accountable outcomes.

Agentic Delivery is the category. MPLP is the lifecycle protocol path within that category.

MPLP is the lifecycle protocol path for making Agentic Delivery explicit, governable, and auditable.

Multi-Agent Lifecycle Governance is the multi-agent form of Agentic Delivery.

Confirmation Boundary.

Evidence Chain.

Semantic Loss.

Semantic Loss is the failure mode. Evidence Chain is the governance response.

PSG / AEL / VSL are reserved runtime substrates for future technical deep-dives.

Cognitive OS, SoloCrew, and Validation Lab form the concrete proof path. MPLP is not placed in the proof path.

This file is a concise content map for AI crawlers and readers. It does not guarantee ranking, citation, or inclusion by any AI system.

## Core Concepts

- AI Agent Lifecycle: https://www.jearonwong.com/concepts/ai-agent-lifecycle/
- Agentic Delivery: https://www.jearonwong.com/concepts/agentic-delivery/
- Agentic Lifecycle Governance: https://www.jearonwong.com/concepts/agentic-lifecycle-governance/
  Agentic Lifecycle Governance explains why AI agent compliance cannot stop at model governance. It treats compliance as lifecycle responsibility across authorization, evidence, accepted outcome, dispute, remediation, and substitution. It introduces Missing Regulatory Objects, RCCS-M, ALCS, and MPLP as one protocol path.
- Missing Regulatory Objects: https://www.jearonwong.com/concepts/missing-regulatory-objects/
  Missing Regulatory Objects are lifecycle responsibility objects that model-centric governance does not consistently define for AI agent and multi-agent systems.
- RCCS-M: https://www.jearonwong.com/concepts/rccs-m/
  RCCS-M is the MRO-adjusted Regulatory Compliance Coverage Score; it is an author-analytical adequacy model, not current law, certification, regulator approval, or procurement ranking.
- ALCS: https://www.jearonwong.com/concepts/alcs/
  ALCS is the Agentic Lifecycle Conformance Score for assessing whether lifecycle responsibility stays coherent across intent, authority, evidence, accepted outcome, dispute, remediation, and closure.
- Lifecycle Responsibility Objects: https://www.jearonwong.com/concepts/lifecycle-responsibility-objects/
  Lifecycle Responsibility Objects keep agent work tied to authority, evidence, accepted outcome, substitution, dispute, remediation, and closure.
- Accepted Outcome: https://www.jearonwong.com/concepts/accepted-outcome/
  Accepted Outcome is the lifecycle point where agent work becomes reviewable, attributable, and accepted responsibility.
- Authority Boundary: https://www.jearonwong.com/concepts/authority-boundary/
  Authority Boundary defines who may authorize agentic action, under what scope, and with what responsibility record.
- Confirmation Boundary: https://www.jearonwong.com/concepts/confirmation-boundary/
- Evidence Chain: https://www.jearonwong.com/concepts/lifecycle-evidence/
- Multi-Agent Lifecycle Governance: https://www.jearonwong.com/lifecycle/
- Semantic Loss: https://www.jearonwong.com/lifecycle/
- MPLP: https://www.jearonwong.com/projects/mplp/

## Applied Agentic Governance Playbooks

- Playbooks index: https://www.jearonwong.com/playbooks/
  Practical guides for making AI agent and multi-agent workflows more rollbackable, verifiable, auditable, and lifecycle-governed. These are independent lifecycle governance guides, not vendor documentation, certification, legal advice, vendor rankings, or procurement recommendations.
- AI Agent Rollback and Verification: https://www.jearonwong.com/playbooks/ai-agent-rollback-verification/
  Explains why agent rollback requires evidence chain, accepted outcome state, authority boundary, and remediation closure rather than only retry, logs, or version history.
- AI Coding Agent Auditability: https://www.jearonwong.com/playbooks/ai-coding-agent-auditability/
  Maps coding agent work to task intent, plan/change boundary, code diff evidence, test evidence, human acceptance, rollback path, drift, and remediation.
- Human Role to Multi-Agent Responsibility Mapping: https://www.jearonwong.com/playbooks/human-role-to-mas-responsibility/
  Explains why human-in-the-loop is insufficient unless human roles map to lifecycle responsibility, delegated authority, accepted outcome ownership, dispute ownership, and remediation.
- Lifecycle Governance Checklist for OpenAI Agent Workflows: https://www.jearonwong.com/playbooks/openai-agent-governance/
  Independent lifecycle governance checklist for workflows built with OpenAI tooling. It avoids current feature claims and does not imply affiliation, endorsement, certification, or procurement advice.
- Lifecycle Governance Checklist for Anthropic / Claude Agent Workflows: https://www.jearonwong.com/playbooks/anthropic-agent-governance/
  Independent lifecycle governance checklist for workflows built with Anthropic / Claude tooling. It avoids current feature claims and does not imply affiliation, endorsement, certification, or procurement advice.
- Lifecycle Governance Checklist for DeepSeek-Based Agent Workflows: https://www.jearonwong.com/playbooks/deepseek-agent-governance/
  Independent lifecycle governance checklist for DeepSeek-based workflows. It avoids current feature claims and does not imply affiliation, endorsement, certification, or procurement advice.
- Lifecycle Governance Checklist for Kimi-Based Agent Workflows: https://www.jearonwong.com/playbooks/kimi-agent-governance/
  Independent lifecycle governance checklist for Kimi-based workflows. It avoids current feature claims and does not imply affiliation with Moonshot AI / Kimi, endorsement, certification, or procurement advice.
- Harness Engineering for AI Agents: https://www.jearonwong.com/playbooks/harness-engineering-for-ai-agents/
  Defines Harness Engineering as wrapping agent execution with context boundaries, authority boundaries, evidence capture, plan/confirm/trace records, rollback, remediation, and accepted outcome.

## Definitions

Quote-ready definitions for AI Agent Lifecycle, Agentic Delivery, Confirmation Boundary, Evidence Chain, Multi-Agent Systems, and related terms. Each entry has a stable anchor: /definitions/#term-slug.

## Key Definitions

- Lifecycle Responsibility Consensus: https://www.jearonwong.com/definitions/#lifecycle-responsibility-consensus
  Lifecycle Responsibility Consensus is the orchestration-layer mechanism that aligns human intent, role authority, agent execution, evidence, review, and accepted outcome into a traceable delivery relationship.

## Delivery Standard

- Delivery Standard: https://www.jearonwong.com/delivery-standard/
The Delivery Standard defines when AI agent work counts as accountable delivery: scope, authority, evidence, review, accepted outcome, and responsibility traceability. All six conditions must be present.

## AI Agent Governance

- AI Agent Governance: https://www.jearonwong.com/ai-agent-governance/
AI Agent Governance is lifecycle accountability for delegated agent work: intent, authority, confirmation, evidence, review, and accepted outcome. Not RBAC. Not monitoring. Not HITL.
